title: Lesson 63: CTA Security: Designing an Enterprise-Grade Security Model Across Systems
description: The CTA security domain as a design discipline: drawing the shared responsibility line, making one identity provider the single source of truth, applying the four-layer access model, choosing an encryption strategy, and layering controls so a hub that aggregates five systems is not only as safe as its weakest credential.

questions.question: Under the shared responsibility model, which controls does the customer design?
options: The physical data center, the network perimeter, and the platform.
Who may log in, what they may do, and how systems authenticate.
The provider's encryption services and its compliance certificates.
Nothing beyond choosing which cloud platform the company buys.
questions.explanation: The provider secures the cloud; the customer secures the org. That means defining who can log in, what they can do, how data is classified, and how integrations authenticate, rather than inheriting responsibility for controls never designed.

questions.question: A user can open a customer record but must not see the card number on it. Which access layer blocks the field?
options: The organization layer, through login IP ranges and hours.
The object layer, by removing read access to the whole object.
The field layer, through field-level security.
The record layer, by hiding the individual record.
questions.explanation: Field-level security controls whether a user can see and edit each individual field. Access is additive, and the most restrictive layer wins, so hiding the field blocks it regardless of object and record access.

questions.question: A regulated field must be encrypted but does not need to support filtering or sorting. Which encryption choice fits?
options: Deterministic Shield Platform Encryption, because it is the stronger scheme.
Volume-level encryption alone, with no field-level scheme added.
No encryption at rest, relying on encrypted transport instead.
Probabilistic Shield Platform Encryption, since filtering is not needed.
questions.explanation: Probabilistic encryption is the stronger default because identical values do not encrypt to identical ciphertext, and deterministic encryption is reserved for fields that must be filtered or sorted. Since exact-match filtering is not required here, probabilistic fits.
